content.user_title: Harden CTFs Against Cheap LLM Shortcuts
content.value_statement: CTF authors need to reduce shallow model pattern matching without making challenges unfair. This skill reproduces the intended solve, applies a small resistance change, and verifies the result.
actual_capabilities: Reproduce an authorized CTF challenge through its player-facing surface.
Record the vulnerability class, solve path, knowledge, and difficulty band.
Identify one cheap LLM shortcut from observed challenge behavior.
Select and apply a minimal resistance pattern without changing the learning objective.
Verify startup, exploitability, shortcut reduction, and end-to-end flag retrieval.
Produce a concise report with status, cost, difficulty, and verification results.
limitations: It is intended only for authorized CTFs, training labs, and systems.
It does not guarantee resistance against every model or solving strategy.
A fresh-solver check requires an isolated model or reviewer.
It does not replace a full security assessment of the challenge application.

use_cases.title: Improve CTF Challenge Quality
use_cases.description: Review a working challenge and remove one obvious shortcut while preserving its vulnerability and learning objective.

use_cases.title: Validate Training Lab Changes
use_cases.description: Test a small challenge transformation from clean start through successful exploitation and flag retrieval.

use_cases.title: Audit LLM Resistance
use_cases.description: Document whether a challenge requires meaningful observation and hypothesis testing instead of immediate pattern matching.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Review the Challenge
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this authorized CTF challenge. List its vulnerability class, intended solve path, required knowledge, difficulty band, and clean-start procedure.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Find the Shortcut
prompt_templates.prompt: Reproduce the authorized challenge solve through the player-facing surface. Identify one cheap LLM shortcut supported by your observations.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Design a Resistance Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Choose the smallest resistance pattern that reduces the identified shortcut. Check the human-cost gate and preserve the vulnerability, objective, and difficulty band.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Verify and Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Restart from a clean state and verify the transformed challenge end to end. Report the final status, shortcut reduction, added meaningful actions, difficulty, fresh-solver result, and changed files.

output_examples.input: A CTF endpoint exposes a valid object identifier in recent activity, and a receipt endpoint accepts that identifier without authorization.
output_examples.output: Baseline: PASS. Vulnerability: broken object-level authorization. Shortcut: the identifier is visible in one response. Change: split the identifier clue into normal activity behavior. Verification: PASS with one additional observation.

output_examples.input: A proposed transformation adds a five-step state machine and requires guessing a randomized value.
output: Reason: The proposal adds brute force and a multi-stage chain.

output_examples.input: A transformed challenge starts normally, keeps the intended vulnerability, and passes an independent solver check.
output_examples.output: Status: TRANSFORMED PASS. The learning objective remains intact, the shortcut is reduced, and the human difficulty remains in the same band.

best_practices: Begin with a clean baseline solve through the player-facing surface.
Use one small resistance change unless evidence requires a second.
Verify the vulnerability, shortcut reduction, and flag retrieval after every change.
anti_patterns: Do not change a challenge before reproducing its intended solve.
Do not use randomness, brute force, or hidden facts that players cannot discover.
Do not claim LLM resistance from self-review without an independent solver check.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: CTF authors, security educators, and maintainers of authorized training labs can use it.

faq.question: Does it make challenges harder?
faq.answer: It targets cheap model shortcuts while keeping the vulnerability, learning objective, and human difficulty band.

faq.question: Can it modify production systems?
faq.answer: No. Use it only for CTFs, training labs, and systems where testing authorization is explicit.

faq.question: What does the baseline solve prove?
faq.answer: It proves that the original challenge works through the intended player-facing vulnerability.

faq.question: How many resistance changes should it apply?
faq.answer: It defaults to zero or one change, with a second change only when the human-cost gate still passes.

faq.question: Does it guarantee resistance to every AI model?
faq.answer: No. An isolated fresh-solver check provides stronger evidence, but no review guarantees universal resistance.
